_comment: Trashlands: keep FTB Ultimine off the salvage economy.
The rule is narrower than 'everything worldgen places'. Three kinds of block are here:
1. Scrap piles - what a worldgen feature heaps up as a dig-for-scrap target.
2. Surface ground - coarse dirt, mound ground, rubble ground, stained ground. The surface is the board
reclamation and encroachment are played on, so stripping it in one hold is terraforming.
3. Bulk stone - minecraft:deepslate in the overworld, recompile:techno_organic_waste in the
Compacted Depths. Both are their dimension's noise_settings default_block.
MECHANICAL CHECK, ONE DIRECTION ONLY: a Recompile block that extends SortableBlock is sortable
and belongs here. Nine do, and all nine are listed. Do NOT grep for gameplay/*_pulls instead -
CompactedBaleBlock overrides pullTable() to reuse GarbageBlock.HOUSEHOLD_PULLS and never names
a table id, so that grep finds eight and misses it. Use the superclass.
Sortability is sufficient, not necessary: cardboard_pile, bulky_waste and tire have no pull
table and are still kind 1, because they are dug for materials rather than sorted.
Ultimine does nothing on the Depths' TERRAIN, which is correct rather than a gap: the noise
settings and the biome's three features place only techno_organic_waste, slag_rubble,
ancient_sculk, lava and bedrock. But vanilla nether fortresses and bastion remnants DO generate
there (Recompile names compacted_depths in both has_structure tags), and their nether brick and
blackstone are not excluded and do chain. Unexamined rather than decided - see pack_setup.md.
Ultimine ships this tag empty, so replace:false appends rather than overwrites.
This governs BREAKING only. The right-click hoe/shovel paths read ftbultimine:farmland_tillable
and ftbultimine:shovel_flattenable, which ship containing coarse dirt and are NOT overridden.
Add any new Recompile scrap-pile block here when one lands.
